`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Issue dependency chain pattern**: #2245 acts as a "gate check" issue — its job was to validate whether the prerequisite artifacts for #2227 could be produced. By designing the acceptance criteria with an "or documented blocker" clause, the project avoids a deadlock where #2245 stays open forever because external conditions (PDF tooling on this machine) prevent the happy path. The blocker is now recorded as structured data (YAML, not just a comment), so #2227 or any future automation can programmatically check `ready_for_2227` and decide whether to proceed.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why this tree structure works well for this project:**
1. **Metadata-only constraint is explicit at every level** — each issue carries the `blocked-metadata-only` limitation in both the body text and acceptance criteria, preventing scope creep into source-text extraction that isn't available.
2. **Wave ordering matches risk/value gradient** — Wave 1 (OCIMF/CSA) extends directly from the #2227 work already done; Wave 4 (DNV/ABS/IMO/USCG) is saved for last because those are the largest directories that benefit from a stabilized extraction workflow.
3. **`status:plan-review`** on all issues — they're ready for your approval before batch agents pick them up, consistent with the planning workflow gate.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why metadata-only sweeps matter:** This pattern — inventorying files by filename/path metadata without reading content — is a safe way to build a wiki scaffold that can later be promoted once source-text extraction becomes available. The `blocked-metadata-only` marker acts as a circuit breaker: downstream consumers (wiki generators, retrieval pipelines) can filter on it to avoid treating these stubs as authoritative. The family grouping step (parent/fragment/merge) prevents wiki-page proliferation — without it, the 7 LR Classification News PDFs or 5 LR Offshore Units notices would each become separate wiki entries instead of being consolidated.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why parent-centric merging matters here:** The OCIMF (MEG 4) directory is a perfect example of "fragment proliferation" — one 297-page parent PDF surrounded by 50 individual page scans, figure extracts, and section slices. Without family grouping, this wave would have generated 51 wiki stubs for what is conceptually a single document. The merge-into-parent strategy reduces this to 1 stub that lists its 50 associated fragments, making the wiki navigable rather than noisy.

**DRM diversity across CSA:** The 5 CSA files use two different DRM systems — Vitrium (4 files) and FileOpen/FOPN (1 file). Vitrium at least allows `pdfinfo` to read page counts and creation dates; FileOpen blocks even that, making CSA 22.1-12 the only stub with "unknown" page count.
